newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: USA Global plans Internet telephony in Australia.
newsitem.headline: USA Global plans Internet telephony in Australia.

text.p: Discount telecommunications service group USA Global Link said on Wednesday it planned to launch its Internet-based telephone service in Australia during the next three months.

USA Global president Larry Chroman told reporters that the privately-held group planned to spend US$40 million on setting up its Australian service and was looking for local partners, either telecommunications groups or Internet Service Providers.
Chroman said he expected USA Global Link to become a significant player in Australia's telephone market as the group would offer customers call discounts of 80 to 90 percent.
"In the next five years,...we hope to have 10 to 15 percent of the whole (long distance) market," said Chroman said.

Australia's A$15 billion telephony market is dominated by government owned Telestra Corp, which is expected to be partially floated later this year after the local telecommunications market is deregulated on July 1.

Chroman said the group's customers would be able to make phone calls to anyone, anywhere in the world, for a fraction of conventional long distance costs. He said calls can be transformed from analogue to digital signals and transmitted via the Internet to any telephone in the world.
Chroman said the group would target medium-sized business and high-use residential customers.
USA Global Link planned to invest US$500 million on its global system and planned an initial public share offering in the 1997 fourth quarter.
